ashley: FYI escalation from Acme — customer reporting intermittent 401s and occasional high latency (p95 >5s) on generate calls starting ~2025-03-01T18:02Z. They’re using SDK v0.9 via an env var service token.

ashley: Attached one request id from their logs: req_20250301_abc123. They also included this header from one response: X-Redwood-Request: 01E8XYZ...

mike: Thanks. Can we get a minimal curl repro they used? ask them to include an explicit X-Request-ID header so we can correlate. Example to share with them: 

```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED
curl -v -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: req_$(date +%s)_customer" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

mike: Ask them to paste full response headers + body and the exact curl output.

ashley: They sent back a short snippet but not reproducible yet. Here’s what they ran (from their support ticket):

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"test"}' -v
```

prasanna: That helps. Please ask them to run these minimal SDK scripts (Python/Node/Go) — ask them to run with an env var set and attach stdout/stderr and any request ids.

Python (requests):

```python
# minimal_repro.py
import os
import requests

KEY = os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
url = "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate"
headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "X-Request-ID": "repro-py-" + str(int(__import__('time').time()))
}
json = {"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello from python"}
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=json, timeout=15)
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.headers)
print(resp.text)
```

Node (fetch):

```js
// minimal_repro.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Request-ID': 'repro-js-' + Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({model: 'redwood-1', input: 'hello from node'})
  });
  console.log(res.status);
  console.log(Object.fromEntries(res.headers));
  console.log(await res.text());
})();
```

Go (net/http):

```go
// minimal_repro.go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
  "time"
)
func main() {
  key := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  body := []byte(`{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello from go"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-ID", "repro-go-"+fmt.Sprint(time.Now().Unix()))
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("err:", err); return }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  fmt.Println("status:", resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println("headers:", resp.Header)
}
```

prasanna: If they still get 401s with the exact same key, request id and timestamp, ask them to also run the curl and paste response headers — we want the WWW-Authenticate header and any body error code. 401s usually mean token revoked/rotated or clock skew if it's signed short-lived token.

jen: Also check billing/usage side — can you confirm the customer org hasn’t hit a billing block? If they’re using a service token bound to a project that had a billing interruption we’ll see auth errors.

ashley: Will ask them to confirm billing and run the three repros above. Requested they include: 1) the X-Request-ID they used, 2) full curl -v output, 3) stdout/stderr of SDK scripts, 4) any server-side request ids we gave in logs (the req_20250301_abc123).

sre-bot: [alert] region-us-west inference p95 crossed 3s between 2025-03-01T18:59Z and 2025-03-01T19:10Z for service inference-rt. Correlation keys: ingress-20250301-18:59, hostpool-gpu-a1.

mike: If they send back a repro that reproduces the 401, we’ll need the exact request-id header value (not just our logged id) so SRE can grep ingress logs. Also ask them to run one repro while we tail the ingress logs so we can capture the full request path and backend response.

ashley: I’ve asked them to run repros now and to upload a debug bundle per our guide: https://internal.redwood/docs/support/debug-bundles — asked to include the three request ids and timestamp. Will paste results here when they come back. :handshake:

mike: Quick triage checklist for us while we wait: confirm token not expired, confirm org billing active, check routing/firewall if they’re on a VPC, check ingress p95 from sre dashboard for matching window, and if latency 401s coincide with high p95 then treat as capacity/circuit issue.
